label: copy-phase input g/f/u/o (rare, unexplained trigger)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never on original tokens or the delimiter, and about 92% of activation mass falls on steps whose input (the token just echoed back) is g, f, u or o (g 40%, f 24%, u 16%, o 12%; h is a small extra). This is only a necessary condition: those steps are active about 0.2% of the time. Activations are weak (mean 0.12, max 0.20) and enriched when f is the current or next output (lift about 20x), e.g. the strongest is f f 1 <DEL> [f] f. Even so, requiring f in the next few outputs gives only 2-4% precision and drops recall to about 60%. Neither in_count, prev_tok, recall position nor first_tok separates active from inactive steps. Never fires at recall_idx 0 and rarely on the last output. No simple predicate explains it.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=g (+5.61), phase=2 & in_tok=f (+4.68), phase=2 & in_tok=u (+4.40), phase=2 & out_tok=f (+3.85), phase=2 & in_tok=o (+3.74), phase=2 & out_tok=u (+3.45). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.43), next_out=- (-2.81), orig1=y (-1.49), t=7 (-1.34).
